`abstract class UIStore`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.ui.core.hook.store` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [UIStore.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/ui/core/hook/store/UIStore.java)

Base class of a store, a container of values that lives as long as its scope and that several UIs can share.

## Description

Annotate the subclass with [`UIStoreData`](/reference/ui/uistoredata/) and get it with [`UI.useStore`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-useStore) or [`Node.useStore`](/reference/nodes/node/#Node-method-useStore).
A `PERMANENT` store is read from the data folder when it is created and written back when a UI closes and when the JVM stops.

## Method details

<a id="UIStore-method-save"></a>

### save

`void save()` 

Writes a `PERMANENT` store to its file now; a store of another scope ignores it.

<a id="UIStore-method-toJson"></a>

### toJson

`Map<String,Object> toJson()` 

Returns the values to save for a `PERMANENT` store, as a map that JOID writes as JSON: numbers, texts, booleans, maps, lists and arrays, and any other object field by field.
A `toJson()` that throws prints a warning, and the other stores are saved anyway.

<a id="UIStore-method-getData"></a>

### getData

`UIStoreData getData()` 

The `@UIStoreData` annotation of the store.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` when the class has none.

<a id="UIStore-method-init"></a>

### init

`void init()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span>

Fills the store with its starting values.
JOID calls it once, right after the factory creates the store and before `fromJson`.

<a id="UIStore-method-destroy"></a>

### destroy

`void destroy()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span>

Releases what the store holds when its scope ends: JOID calls it for a `LOCAL` store when the UI that holds it closes.
A `destroy()` that throws prints a warning, and the store is forgotten anyway.

<a id="UIStore-method-fromJson"></a>

### fromJson

`void fromJson(Map<String,Object> json)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span>

Restores the values that `toJson()` saved, right after `init()`.
The map holds the types of JSON: `Long` and `Double` for the numbers, `Boolean`, `String`, `List<Object>` and `Map<String, Object>`.
A `fromJson()` that throws prints a warning, keeps a copy of the file aside, and the store starts again from `init()`.
